summary: The Marine Scholarship of China supports master's and doctoral study in oceanography and related marine-affairs fields in China. It was started jointly by the State Oceanic Administration and the Ministry of Education, and the China Scholarship Council handles admissions and routine management. It is for non-Chinese citizens in good health from coastal or island countries around the South China Sea, the Indian Ocean and the Pacific, and from developing countries in Africa. It gives tuition, housing (or a housing subsidy), a monthly living allowance and medical insurance, for a maximum of 4 years. Each host university (for example Tongji University and Xiamen University) publishes its own guide and takes the applications.
eligibility_notes:
Nationality: the applicant must be a non-Chinese citizen in good health. The citizen must come from a coastal or island country of the South China Sea, the Indian Ocean, or the Pacific and its surrounding island countries, or from a developing country in Africa. Xiamen University also names developing countries in the Americas. The notices describe regions, not a list of countries.

Education: master's applicants need a bachelor's degree in a related field. Doctoral applicants need a master's degree in a related field. The applicant must apply for an ocean-related postgraduate programme. People who already work in oceanographic or related sectors get priority (Xiamen).

Age: see the age note. The limits differ between the host university notices read, and the word 'usually' is used at Tongji.

Language: for Chinese-taught programmes at Tongji, a valid HSK level 5 certificate with a total score of at least 180 is required. If the highest degree was taught in Chinese, a certificate saying so replaces the HSK. For programmes taught in other languages, the language certificates the university asks for (for example IELTS or TOEFL) are needed. Applicants from English-speaking countries do not need English proof (Tongji appendix). At Xiamen, an HSK certificate is asked for only when the applicant wants remedial Chinese before the main subject: HSK level 4 with at least 180 points for law programmes, and HSK level 3 with at least 180 points for science and engineering programmes. The required HSK level must be passed within the first year. Xiamen's general guide also sets entry scores for its programmes: for Chinese-taught programmes HSK 5 with 210 or more (humanities, economics, management, law, arts) or HSK 4 with 210 or more (science, engineering, medicine, sport), and for English-taught programmes TOEFL iBT 80 or IELTS 6.0, or a certificate that the previous degree was taught in English.

Admission first: the applicant must be admitted (or accepted by an advisor) by the host university. Tongji asks the applicant to hold an acceptance letter from a Tongji advisor before applying. Xiamen considers the scholarship only after admission.

Maximum support: 4 years in total.
age_experience_notes: Age limits are not the same in the notices read. Tongji's 2026 notice says a master's applicant is usually under 35 and a doctoral applicant usually under 40. Tongji's 2025 notice and Xiamen's notice give under 40 (master's) and under 45 (doctoral); Xiamen measures this on 1 September of the academic year. Work experience in an ocean-related sector gives priority at Xiamen; no minimum years of experience are stated.
funding_summary: Each award covers the tuition fee, accommodation (free on-campus housing, or an off-campus housing subsidy), a monthly living allowance of RMB 3,000 for master's students or RMB 3,500 for doctoral students, and comprehensive medical insurance. International travel and other study costs are paid by the student. Support lasts for the length of the programme, with a maximum of 4 years. Master's programmes last 2 to 3 years and doctoral programmes 4 years. Recipients take part in an annual review to keep the award (Xiamen).
programmes_note: Tongji names marine science, geophysics and other marine-affairs related majors, mainly in four schools: the School of Ocean and Earth Science, the School of Environmental Science and Engineering, the School of Civil Engineering and the College of Electronics and Information Engineering. Xiamen University publishes a table of programmes by teaching medium (Chinese or English) and level; the list is given below. Ocean University of China also hosts the scholarship, but its programme details were not available.
institutions_note: The China Scholarship Council handles admissions and routine management. Applicants apply to a host university under the Type B route of the CSC online system, using the university's agency number, and are considered after the university admits them. The host universities whose guides were read are Tongji University (agency number 10247) and Xiamen University (agency number 10384). Ocean University of China also announced the scheme for 2027/2028; its details were not read. Other host universities may exist. Each university has its own online application system, documents and contact.

summary.detail: Master's study in oceanography or related fields. A related bachelor's degree is required. Programmes last 2 to 3 years (Xiamen's general guide gives 3 years for Chinese-taught and 2 years for English-taught programmes). Living allowance RMB 3,000 per month. Xiamen: off-campus housing subsidy RMB 700 per month.

benefits.conditions: For the length of the programme, with a maximum of 4 years of support in total.

benefits.limit_text: Free on-campus housing, or an off-campus housing subsidy (Xiamen: RMB 700 per month for master's, RMB 1,000 per month for doctoral)
benefits.conditions: Tongji's notice gives no subsidy amount. At Xiamen the student pays the security deposit and the utilities for on-campus housing.

benefits.limit_text: RMB 3,000 per month (master's); RMB 3,500 per month (doctoral)
benefits.conditions: Recipients take part in an annual review; those who fail it are suspended or lose the award (Xiamen).
The student pays for international travel.

benefits.limit_text: Physical examination, course materials and other study costs not covered
benefits.conditions: Xiamen lists the physical examination, the on-campus housing deposit and utilities, and course materials as paid by the recipient. Tongji says other study expenses are paid by the recipient.

requirements.text: Application Form for Chinese Government Scholarship, created in the CSC online application system (Type B), completed in Chinese or English, printed and signed by the applicant. Tongji's appendix asks for 2 signed copies; Xiamen asks for a scan to upload.

Application form for international students from the host university's own online system, printed and signed (Tongji asks for 2 copies). Xiamen takes the scholarship scan inside its own online application.

Highest degree certificate. A certificate in Chinese or English may be a photocopy. A certificate in another language must be notarised by a Chinese embassy or consulate abroad (or an embassy or consulate in China) and come with a notarised Chinese or English translation. Expected graduates need an official proof from their institution of their status and the date the degree will be awarded.

Academic transcripts: original, with all courses, signed or sealed by the issuing authority. A photocopy without signature or seal is not accepted. A transcript in another language needs a notarised translation as above.
The applicant's study or research plan in China, in Chinese or English.
requirements.conditional_rule: Listed in Tongji's appendix; Xiamen's general guide asks for a study plan inside a personal statement of at least 1,000 words

requirements.text: Two letters of recommendation, in Chinese or English, from professors or associate professors. Xiamen's guide asks that they are signed or stamped and show the recommender's name, employer, position and contact details.

Photocopy of the Foreigner Physical Examination Form from the CSC, completed in Chinese or English. Every test on the form must be done; a blank section, a missing doctor signature or a missing hospital seal makes the form invalid. Xiamen's general guide asks for a physical examination record valid for 6 months.

Proof of language ability. For Chinese-taught programmes: HSK level 5 with a total score of 180 or more (Tongji), or a certificate that the highest degree was taught in Chinese. For English-taught programmes: official proof of English ability, not needed for applicants from English-speaking countries (Tongji). Xiamen asks for an HSK certificate only for applicants who want remedial Chinese, and its general guide gives TOEFL iBT 80 or IELTS 6.0 for English-taught programmes.
Copy of the passport. Xiamen asks for the passport page, valid at least through 31 October 2027, in its 2027 intake guides.

Personal statement and CV. Xiamen's general guide asks for a personal statement of at least 1,000 words (self-introduction, education, motivation, study plan, career goals), written in Chinese for Chinese-taught programmes and in English for English-taught ones.
Acceptance letter from an advisor of Tongji University. Tongji asks applicants to hold admission from an advisor and to know the major before they apply.
requirements.conditional_rule: Tongji applicants. Xiamen's pre-acceptance letter is optional but gives admission priority.

requirements.text: Other proof of academic achievements, if any. Xiamen's general guide also lists: birth certificate, parents' identity documents, a financial support guarantee statement, and a no-criminal-record report issued within 6 months before submission.
requirements.conditional_rule: Tongji: optional. Xiamen general guide items apply to Xiamen applicants.

application_steps.title: Choose a host university and secure admission or an advisor
application_steps.detail: Pick an ocean-related master's or doctoral programme at a host university such as Tongji or Xiamen. Tongji asks you to hold an acceptance letter from one of its advisors and to know your major before you apply. Xiamen considers the scholarship only after the university admits you.

application_steps.title: Apply in the CSC online system as Type B
application_steps.detail: In the CSC online application system choose Program Category Type B and enter the university's agency number (Tongji 10247, Xiamen 10384). Choose the Marine Scholarship of China as the scholarship type. Print the Application Form for Chinese Government Scholarship, complete it in Chinese or English, and sign it.

application_steps.title: Complete the university's own online application
application_steps.detail: Make a second online application in the host university's system. At Tongji, print and sign the Application Form for International Students and email electronic copies of all appendix documents to the contact person. At Xiamen, upload the scan of the signed scholarship form in the Xiamen system; no paper documents need to be mailed. The Xiamen application fee is RMB 400, as stated in its master's and doctoral guides.

application_steps.title: University expert panel reviews the application
application_steps.detail: Tongji's expert panel looks at education background, academic ability, research achievements, the opinion of the supervisor and related work experience. Xiamen's review looks at professional background, academic record, work experience, language, overall merit, research achievements and the supervisor's comments. Xiamen's guides also describe a qualification check and an academic assessment, which can be a remote interview or a written exam.

application_steps.title: Final approval by the Ministry of Natural Resources and CSC
application_steps.detail: The host university sends its shortlisted candidates to China's Ministry of Natural Resources and the China Scholarship Council for final approval. Tongji's 2026 notice expected final results around May 2026. Xiamen publishes final results on its admissions site in July and August.

application_steps.title: Receive the admission notice and visa form
application_steps.detail: Tongji sends the Admission Notice and the Visa Application Form (JW201) to awardees as soon as possible after the results. Applicants who need remedial Chinese at Xiamen must pass the required HSK level within the first year, then meet the programme's entry requirements before starting the main subject.

application_steps.title: Pass the annual review to keep the award
application_steps.detail: Recipients take part in an annual review under the scholarship's management rules. Those who pass can keep the scholarship for the next academic year; those who fail are suspended or disqualified. Recipients pay the costs the scholarship does not cover, such as international travel and the physical examination. Total support is at most 4 years.

fetch_problems: Tongji's 2027 notice page was read, but both of its attachments (the main notice and the appendix) require a verification code to download and could not be opened. The 2026 notice and appendix were used instead, so 2027 conditions may differ (for example the age limits).
Ocean University of China's announcement page only points to a separate 'High Level Graduate Student' programme page that was not linked; its Marine Scholarship details could not be read.

The English-medium programme table on Xiamen's page is hard to read as text; the level assigned to some English-taught programmes was taken from the way it was extracted and should be checked by an editor.
notes: Age limits conflict between sources: Tongji's 2026 notice says usually under 35 (master's) and under 40 (doctoral), while Tongji's 2025 notice and Xiamen's 2026 guide say under 40 and under 45. The stored data (40/45 for Tongji) matched the 2025 notice. Check Tongji's 2027 notice when it can be read.

The Xiamen guide read describes the 2026 intake. Xiamen's master's and doctoral guides read for the general rules describe the 2027 intake; their documents list is for Xiamen's regular admission and is carried into the Xiamen rows above as general rules.

Language levels differ by university: Tongji says HSK 5 (180+) for Chinese-taught programmes, while Xiamen asks HSK only for remedial Chinese (level 4 for law, level 3 for science and engineering, 180+ points) in the scholarship guide and sets HSK 5 or 4 with 210+ points in its general guide.
